title: Testing Package Basics
intro: Testing in Go is built into the standard library and the toolchain — you do not need a testing framework to write good tests. This module covers the _test.go file naming convention (only compiled during test runs), the TestXxx naming rule (must start with Test, take *testing.T, return nothing), t.Error and t.Logf for reporting failures without stopping the test vs t.Fatal and t.Fatalf for stopping immediately (the distinction matters when you have multiple assertions), the table-driven test pattern (a slice of struct test cases — the idiomatic Go way to avoid duplicated test functions), running tests with go test ./..., go test -v for verbose output, go test -run TestFunctionName to run a specific test, go test -cover for coverage reporting, and example functions (ExampleFunctionName runs as a test and doubles as documentation). These basics cover 80% of what Go freshers need to write and understand tests in a Go codebase.
